In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of high dose glucocortocid treatment and burn injury results in a significant reduction in the lung macrophage population, and the remaining cells are severely compromised in their ability to phagocytize bacteria.
high dose glucorticoid treatment and/or burn injury results in an impaired alveolar macro-phage population in the lower tract and a decreased functional activity of the remaining phagocytic cells.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endogenous glucocorticoids released following burn injury are sufficient to impair the lung phagocytosis of alveolar macrohages.
high dose cortisol treatment and burn injury result in an impairment in the lung phagocytosis.

high dose cortisone treatment, burn injury or the combination of both resulted in severe alterations in lung macrophage function and a marked elevation of cortisol concentrations in the plasma and lung lavages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
burn injury and cortisone therapy result in an increased risk of infection in the lung due to a marked impairment in the phagocytic function of the resident alveolar macrophase population.

the combination of a reduced alveolar macro phage population and an impaired macrophage functional activity in the lung following burn injury or high dose cortisone treatment may result in a compromised host defense mechanism against pulmonary infections.

burn injury and glucocorticoid administration can severely impair the functional activity of resident macrophages in the lung, which may be due in part to the increased endogenous levels of cortisone in the lung.
